title: Viewport handoff & canvas fallback for charts, tables and stacked modals
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem statement: several console surfaces (Cost Explorer charts, rollouts table and stacked modals) were exhibiting janky reflow, scroll jumps, and rendering artifacts across Safari and older Firefox on macOS when panels change height or when charts repaint during quick vertical scrolls. Mobile gestures were being interrupted by modal stacking changes and the existing canvas chart rendering produced gaps on Safari 15/16 when GPU-backed canvas is throttled.

Goal: produce a resilient layout strategy (viewport handoff + flexbox/position handoff), fallback rendering approach for charts (SVG fallback when canvas fails), and a modal stacking policy that avoids scroll lock and maintains keyboard focus/ARIA semantics. Deliverables: interactive Figma prototype, runnable QA checklist, cross-browser test plan, implementation handoff with tokenized CSS breakpoints and a lightweight performance regression harness (trace links).
design_notes: Key decisions made in prototype: 1) Use explicit viewport handoff: for major panel transitions we transition from position:relative/flex to position:fixed at a single anchor point to avoid layout thrash; this minimizes reflow when side panels collapse/expand. 2) Charts should attempt WebGL/canvas render first and gracefully degrade to SVG when paint fails more than twice within a 3s window (heuristic tuned in prototype). 3) Modal stacking: introduce an 'inert background' utility and an ordered z-index set (1000, 1100, 1200) with visual stacking gutters; stacked modals use transform: translateZ(0) sparingly to avoid forcing compositor layers. 4) Touch/gesture UX: when a modal is opened from a bottom sheet on mobile, we shadow the underlying scroll container and route pan gestures to the top modal; if the modal height changes >20% during an interaction we snapshot scroll position and animate a gentle anchor to avoid content jump. 5) Accessibility: maintain focus trap policy, ensure aria-hidden applied to background when inert applied, and provide announceable progress when canvas->SVG fallback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Cost Explorer charts do not produce visible blank-pixel gaps in latest Safari and Firefox when performing rapid scrolls on macOS
Opening/closing side panels during active table scroll does not cause >8px unexpected content jump on desktop or mobile
Stacked modals maintain keyboard focus order and screen reader perceives only active modal as dialog
Canvas fallback to SVG occurs within 2s of repeated paint failures and is logged for dev telemetry
Regression dashboard shows no >10% increase in main-thread time for affected pages after changes
steps_for_review: Review Figma prototype flows (desktop/tablet/mobile) and comment on the anchor/hand-off patterns
Run the attached QA script in nightly build on Chrome, Safari 16, Firefox 115, Edge and iOS Safari
Verify ARIA and focus behavior using VoiceOver (macOS) and TalkBack (Android) on sample pages
Check telemetry sample for canvas fallback events in staging (link in attachments)
ua_test_plan: macOS: Chrome latest, Safari 16, Firefox 115 — reproduce rapid vertical scroll while toggling right-side panel
Windows: Edge latest, Chrome latest — verify modal stacking and keyboard navigation
iOS: Safari on iPhone 13/14 — bottom-sheet to stacked modal transition and pan/gesture handoff
Android: Chrome and Samsung Browser — verify inert background and focus trap during nested modals
notes_from_review: Design review 2026-03-03: engineering raised an implementation risk for painting heuristics — we agreed to expose the fallback threshold as a remote config flag and to ship a canary behind the 'resilience' feature flag. Accessibility review 2026-03-05: confirm that 'inert' polyfill doesn't interfere with automated test runners; add explicit aria-live announcement for 'render mode changed' events.

Create CSS token PR with named breakpoints and handoff utilities (DES -> ENG handoff)

Schedule cross-team QA session week of 2026-03-15
